strings.d1.s0.name: Plaza de Mayo
strings.d1.s0.tips: Casa Rosada (the pink palace, free tours at weekends), the Cathedral (Pope Francis's former church), and the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo on Thursdays at 15:30.
strings.d1.s1.name: Café Tortoni
strings.d1.s1.tips: A café since 1858: order churros and hot chocolate. Expect a queue. On Avenida de Mayo.
strings.d1.s2.name: San Telmo Market
strings.d1.s2.tips: A market dating from 1897, with choripán (grilled sausage sandwich) and empanada stalls and antique dealers. On Sundays the Defensa street fair stretches over 10 blocks.
strings.d1.s3.name: Plaza Dorrego
strings.d1.s3.tips: Street tango on Sundays and antique shops.
strings.d1.s4.name: El Zanjón de Granados
strings.d1.s4.tips: 1730 tunnels beneath a restored mansion; visit by guided tour.
strings.d1.b0.name: La Brigada San Telmo
strings.d1.b0.tips: A parrilla (steakhouse) with football decor, where the meat is cut with a spoon.
strings.d1.b1.name: Museo Histórico Nacional
strings.d1.b1.tips: National history in Parque Lezama; free. An alternative to Zanjón.
strings.d2.s0.name: Recoleta Cemetery
strings.d2.s0.tips: A city of marble mausoleums with Evita's tomb (Duarte) and plenty of cats. Free, though foreigners have needed a 14,000 ARS ticket since 2025.
strings.d2.s1.name: Floralis Genérica
strings.d2.s1.tips: A giant steel flower that opens and closes with the sun; at Plaza Naciones Unidas.
strings.d2.s2.name: MALBA
strings.d2.s2.tips: Latin American art, including Frida Kahlo and Berni. Discounted entry on Wednesdays.
strings.d2.s3.name: Bosques de Palermo & Rosedal
strings.d2.s3.tips: A rose garden and lakes; rent a rowing boat or a bike.
strings.d2.s4.name: Don Julio
strings.d2.s4.tips: Billed as the world's best steakhouse. Without a reservation, join the queue at 18:45 (champagne is on the house). Order the bife de chorizo and a malbec.
strings.d2.b0.name: El Preferido de Palermo
strings.d2.b0.tips: Don Julio's pink sibling, serving milanesa (breaded cutlet) and tapas.
strings.d2.b1.name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes
strings.d2.b1.tips: Free entry; Rodin, Monet, in Recoleta.
strings.d3.s0.name: Caminito
strings.d3.s0.tips: Colourful corrugated-iron houses and street tango. Go during the day and don't stray from the main streets.
strings.d3.s1.name: La Bombonera Boca Juniors
strings.d3.s1.tips: Stadium and museum tour; a shrine to Maradona.
strings.d3.s2.name: El Obrero La Boca
strings.d3.s2.tips: A workers' canteen from 1954 serving milanesa and tortilla. Bono has eaten here.
strings.d3.s3.name: Puerto Madero Puente de la Mujer
strings.d3.s3.tips: Calatrava's bridge and the old port, plus the Fragata Sarmiento ship.
strings.d3.s4.name: Reserva Ecológica Costanera Sur
strings.d3.s4.tips: A nature reserve on the Rio de la Plata shore. Come for sunset; choripán stands are outside.
strings.d3.b0.name: Cabaña Las Lilas Puerto Madero
strings.d3.b1.name: Usina del Arte
strings.d3.b1.tips: A concert hall and gallery in a former power station; in La Boca, free.
strings.d4.s0.name: Tren de la Costa Tigre
strings.d4.s0.tips: One hour from Retiro on the Mitre line (the scenic alternative is the Tren de la Costa). Ends at the Tigre pier.
strings.d4.s1.name: Puerto de Frutos
strings.d4.s1.tips: A market at the old fruit port selling wicker, woodwork and mate gourds.
strings.d4.s2.name: Tigre Delta Boat Tour
strings.d4.s2.tips: The channels of the Paraná delta, with floating houses and market boats. The Interisleña public boat is cheap.
strings.d4.s3.name: Museo de Arte Tigre
strings.d4.s3.tips: The 1912 Tigre Club palace, a Belle Époque building on the riverbank.
strings.d4.s4.name: María Luján Tigre
strings.d4.s4.tips: A riverside parrilla with asado and views.
strings.d4.b0.name: Museo del Mate
strings.d4.b0.tips: A mate museum with tastings; in Tigre.
strings.d4.b1.name: Almacén de Ramos Generales Tigre
strings.d4.b1.tips: A former general store turned restaurant; try the picada (sharing platter).
strings.d5.s0.name: Buquebus Colonia Feribotu
strings.d5.s0.tips: A 1 hour 15 minute ferry (bring your passport; about 70,000 ARS return online) to Uruguay.
strings.d5.s1.name: Barrio Histórico Colonia
strings.d5.s1.tips: A UNESCO-listed Portuguese-Spanish town with Calle de los Suspiros and the Portuguese gate.
strings.d5.s2.name: Faro de Colonia
strings.d5.s2.tips: A lighthouse from 1857 with views over the Rio de la Plata (UYU cash).
strings.d5.s3.name: Charco Bistró Colonia
strings.d5.s3.tips: A riverside bistro; try the chivito (Uruguayan steak sandwich). Pay in UYU or USD.
strings.d5.s4.name: Rambla & Plaza Mayor
strings.d5.s4.tips: The waterfront road, with classic cars. Ferries before sunset run between 17:00 and 19:00.
strings.d5.b0.name: Museo Portugués Colonia
strings.d5.b0.tips: A museum of the Portuguese era; an alternative to the lighthouse.
strings.d5.b1.name: El Buen Suspiro Colonia
strings.d5.b1.tips: Wine and picada on Calle de los Suspiros.
strings.d6.s0.name: Palermo Soho Plaza Serrano
strings.d6.s0.tips: Boutiques and murals, with a design market at weekends.
strings.d6.s1.name: La Cabrera Palermo
strings.d6.s1.tips: Parrilla with 15 small side dishes; 40% off during happy hour, 12:00-13:30.
strings.d6.s2.name: Museo Evita
strings.d6.s2.tips: Evita's clothes and life story, in a Palermo mansion.
strings.d6.s3.name: El Ateneo Grand Splendid
strings.d6.s3.tips: A bookshop in a former theatre, often called the world's most beautiful. On Santa Fe.
strings.d6.s4.name: Tango Show El Viejo Almacén
strings.d6.s4.tips: San Telmo's most traditional tango show, with a dinner package; or go to a milonga (La Viruta is cheap).
strings.d6.b0.name: La Viruta Milonga
strings.d6.b0.tips: A milonga (tango dance night) where locals dance; lesson plus night out.
strings.d6.b1.name: Sarkis Palermo
strings.d6.b1.tips: Armenian meze, an alternative to the parrilla; expect a queue.
strings.d7.theme: Teatro Colón and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Teatro Colón
strings.d7.s0.tips: An opera house with some of the world's best acoustics. English tours run every hour; don't miss the golden hall.
strings.d7.s1.name: Obelisco & Avenida 9 de Julio
strings.d7.s1.tips: The world's widest avenue and the obelisk, the symbol of Buenos Aires.
strings.d7.s2.name: Confitería La Ideal
strings.d7.s2.tips: A restored café from 1912; medialunas (small croissants) and café con leche for your farewell.
strings.d7.s3.name: Galerías Pacífico
strings.d7.s3.tips: A shopping centre with a frescoed dome; leather souvenirs (Calle Florida).
strings.d7.s4.name: Ezeiza Havalimanı Tienda León
strings.d7.s4.tips: One hour by bus or taxi; farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Museo de Arte Decorativo
strings.d7.b0.tips: The Errázuriz palace; an alternative to the Colón.
strings.d7.b1.name: Las Violetas Almagro
strings.note0: Get a SUBE card (from kiosks). The metro (Subte) and buses (colectivo) are cheap, and Uber/Cabify are safe. Ezeiza is 1 hour away; Aeroparque is in the city.
strings.note1: October-November: purple jacaranda trees in spring, the best season. December-February: 30-35°C and humid; locals are on holiday and the city is empty. March-May: autumn.
strings.note2: ARS inflation means prices change fast (ASSUMPTION: mid-2026). The 'dólar MEP' rate applied automatically on cards is good; Western Union for cash. The new 100 USD series is the one to bring.
strings.note3: Parrilla 30-60,000 ARS, empanada 2,000, coffee and medialuna 5,000, tango show 90,000+. Tip 10% in cash. Dinner is after 21:00.
strings.note4: Watch for pickpockets: off the main street in Caminito and at the Retiro bus terminal. Don't show your phone in the street. Bring your passport for Colonia.
strings.note5: Shared mate, dulce de leche, alfajores (Havanna), malbec; Recoleta's Sunday market.
